subject: Mechanical Engineering
title: Vacuum Systems: Power from Nothing
description: A fast breakdown of Vacuum Systems: Power from Nothing for builders.

hook.text: A suction cup picks up a glass sheet. No clamps, no magnets — just atmospheric pressure pushing from outside.

buildup.text: A vacuum pump removes air from a sealed space. Atmospheric pressure on the outside does the holding work.

discovery.text: At sea level, atmosphere pushes with about one kilogram per square centimeter. A large cup holds surprising weight.

twist.text: You can't pull harder than one atmosphere. Perfect vacuum is the limit. For more force, you need bigger cups.

climax.text: Robots in car factories lift windshields, circuit boards, and body panels with vacuum grippers. Clean and gentle.

punchline.text: Remove the air. Let the atmosphere do the gripping.

quiz.question: What actually holds objects to a vacuum gripper?
options: The vacuum pump creates a magnetic pull on the object's surface
Atmospheric pressure on the outside pushes the object against the cup
Static electricity generated by air removal attracts the object
